content: पाण्डु {%a.%} Pale-white, whitish, pale, yellowish; यथा पाण्ड्वाविकम् <ls>Bṛ. Up. 2. 3. 6</ls>; विकलकरणः पाण्डुच्छायः शुचा परिदुर्बलः <ls>U. 3. 22</ls>. .{@-ण्डुः@} .²1 The pale-white or yellowish-white colour. .²2 Jaundice. .²3 A white elephant. .²4 <ab>N.</ab> of the father of the Pāṇḍavas. [He was begotten by Vyāsa on Ambālikā, one of the widows of Vicitravīrya. He was called Pāṇḍu, because he was born pale (पाण्डु) by reason of his mother having become quite pale with fear when in private with the sage Vyāsa; (यस्मात् पाण्डुत्वमापन्ना विरूपं प्रेक्ष्य मामिह . तस्मादेव सुतस्ते वै पाण्डुरेव भविष्यति <ls>Mb.</ls>) He was prevented by a curse from having progeny himself; so he allowed his first wife Kuntī to make use of a charm she had acquired from Durvāsas for the birth of sons. She gave birth to Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma and Arjuna; and Mādrī, his other wife, by the use of the same charm, gave birth to Nakula and Sahadeva. One day Pāṇdu forgot the curse under which he was labouring, and made bold to embrace Mādrī, but he fell immediately dead in her arms.]
